I was originally considering the basic design of the Media dishwasher, but I ultimately decided on the window type. The reason was that it had a more open feel, a prettier design, and an added UV sterilization function. The price difference was only about 40,000 won compared to the basic design model. I decided to go with this one because I thought I would use it for a long time once I bought it, and after discussing it with my husband, I decided. Reasonable price. It turned out that various large companies were selling dishwashers manufactured by Media. They were selling them at a higher price with slightly different labels and designs. Knowing that, I wondered if it was really necessary to buy it at a higher price. So I searched for media and found out that Coupang officially imported it and provided 2 years of free A/S, so I bought it. When I tried running the low-noise dishwasher, it was quieter than I thought. Honestly, I was surprised by how quiet it was. Since it's the type that you use on top of the sink, I expected it to be quite noisy. By my standards, it's really quiet. It's perfect for a house with a baby. Cleaning power + convenience. The decisive reason I bought the dishwasher was because I'm seven months pregnant, and now I can't stand still without any pain in my back, hips, stomach, or knees due to the weight of my belly. So, I bought it to reduce the time I spend doing housework, such as washing dishes. I've been using it and it's great because I can do other things during the dishwashing time or take a break when I'm tired. Also, we'll be a family of three soon after the baby is born, and since we mostly eat home-cooked meals rather than eating out, I could see how much better my quality of life would be if the dishwasher cleaned the dishes and bottles more thoroughly than I could. I used it and was very satisfied with the automatic door opening function because I didn't have to wait for the dishwasher to finish and then manually open the door. The glass cups looked even clearer than the ones I washed myself! I cleaned the dishes thoroughly, top, middle, and bottom, three times, so if you play Tetris well, there's no place that's not cleaned. I searched on Coupang and bought some eco-friendly liquid detergent in advance and poured it in. The latest version of Jayeonpong dishwasher-specific liquid detergent has good reviews for its three-fold enhanced cleaning power, in addition to regular dishes. It has a lemony scent that leaves no residue, and it smells good. It's also reasonably priced, so I plan to continue using it. The only downside is that this model doesn't have hot air drying. But since most six-person dishwashers do, I understand and can overlook it. The dishwasher intelligently uses the auto-open feature to release heat, and after a while, the dishes dry. I didn't have to dry them every time I washed them by hand. And this product has a stainless steel top, so I don't have to worry. This was a big plus, and it played a part in my decision. This is my honest review of a product I purchased with my own money. If it helped you make a purchase, please let me know. Please press and hold! To improve your quality of life, I highly recommend the Media Dishwasher!

I was originally considering the basic design of the Media dishwasher, but I ultimately decided on the window type. The reason was that it had a more open feel, a prettier design, and an added UV sterilization function. The price difference was only about 40,000 won compared to the basic design model. I decided to go with this one because I thought I would use it for a long time once I bought it, and after discussing it with my husband, I decided. Reasonable price. It turned out that various large companies were selling dishwashers manufactured by Media. They were selling them at a higher price with slightly different labels and designs. Knowing that, I wondered if it was really necessary to buy it at a higher price. So I searched for media and found out that Coupang officially imported it and provided 2 years of free A/S, so I bought it. When I tried running the low-noise dishwasher, it was quieter than I thought. Honestly, I was surprised by how quiet it was. The decisive reason I bought the dishwasher was because I'm seven months pregnant, and now I can't stand still without any pain in my back, hips, stomach, or knees due to the weight of my belly. So, I bought it to reduce the time I spend doing housework, such as washing dishes. I've been using it and it's great because I can do other things during the dishwashing time or take a break when I'm tired. Also, we'll be a family of three soon after the baby is born, and since we mostly eat home-cooked meals rather than eating out, I could see how much better my quality of life would be if the dishwasher cleaned the dishes and bottles more thoroughly than I could. I used it and was very satisfied with the automatic door opening function because I didn't have to wait for the dishwasher to finish and then manually open the door. The glass cups looked even clearer than the ones I washed myself! I cleaned the dishes thoroughly, top, middle, and bottom, three times, so if you play Tetris well, there's no place that's not cleaned. I searched on Coupang and bought some eco-friendly liquid detergent in advance and poured it in. The latest version of Jayeonpong dishwasher-specific liquid detergent has good reviews for its three-fold enhanced cleaning power, in addition to regular dishes. It has a lemony scent that leaves no residue, and it smells good. It's also reasonably priced, so I plan to continue using it. The only downside is that this model doesn't have hot air drying. But since most six-person dishwashers do, I understand and can overlook it. The dishwasher intelligently uses the auto-open feature to release heat, and after a while, the dishes dry. I didn't have to dry them every time I washed them by hand. And this product has a stainless steel top, so I don't have to worry. This was a big plus, and it played a part in my decision. This is my honest review of a product I purchased with my own money. If it helped you make a purchase, please let me know. Please press and hold! To improve your quality of life, I highly recommend the Media Dishwasher!

So, I bought it to reduce the time I spend doing housework, such as washing dishes. I've been using it and it's great because I can do other things during the dishwashing time or take a break when I'm tired. I cleaned the dishes thoroughly, top, middle, and bottom, three times, so if you play Tetris well, there's no place that's not cleaned. But since most six-person dishwashers do, I understand and can overlook it. The dishwasher intelligently uses the auto-open feature to release heat, and after a while, the dishes dry. I didn't have to dry them every time I washed them by hand. And this product has a stainless steel top, so I don't have to worry. This was a big plus, and it played a part in my decision. So, I bought it to reduce the time I spend doing housework, such as washing dishes. I've been using it and it's great because I can do other things during the dishwashing time or take a break when I'm tired. I didn't have to dry them every time I washed them by hand. And this product has a stainless steel top, so I don't have to worry. This was a big plus, and it played a part in my decision. Comments (English): My money, my country / Media 6-person dishwasher review. Product basic information. Media 6-person dishwasher with automatic door opening and UV lamp. I was originally considering the basic design of the Media dishwasher, but I ultimately decided on the window type. The reason was that it had a more open feel, a prettier design, and an added UV sterilization function. The price difference was only about 40,000 won compared to the basic design model. I decided to go with this one because I thought I would use it for a long time once I bought it, and after discussing it with my husband, I decided. Reasonable price. It turned out that various large companies were selling dishwashers manufactured by Media. They were selling them at a higher price with slightly different labels and designs. Knowing that, I wondered if it was really necessary to buy it at a higher price. So I searched for media and found out that Coupang officially imported it and provided 2 years of free A/S, so I bought it. When I tried running the low-noise dishwasher, it was quieter than I thought. Honestly, I was surprised by how quiet it was. Since it's the type that you use on top of the sink, I expected it to be quite noisy. By my standards, it's really quiet. It's perfect for a house with a baby. Cleaning power + convenience. The decisive reason I bought the dishwasher was because I'm seven months pregnant, and now I can't stand still without any pain in my back, hips, stomach, or knees due to the weight of my belly. So, I bought it to reduce the time I spend doing housework, such as washing dishes. I've been using it and it's great because I can do other things during the dishwashing time or take a break when I'm tired. Also, we'll be a family of three soon after the baby is born, and since we mostly eat home-cooked meals rather than eating out, I could see how much better my quality of life would be if the dishwasher cleaned the dishes and bottles more thoroughly than I could. I used it and was very satisfied with the automatic door opening function because I didn't have to wait for the dishwasher to finish and then manually open the door. The glass cups looked even clearer than the ones I washed myself! I cleaned the dishes thoroughly, top, middle, and bottom, three times, so if you play Tetris well, there's no place that's not cleaned. I searched on Coupang and bought some eco-friendly liquid detergent in advance and poured it in. The latest version of Jayeonpong dishwasher-specific liquid detergent has good reviews for its three-fold enhanced cleaning power, in addition to regular dishes. But since most six-person dishwashers do, I understand and can overlook it. The dishwasher intelligently uses the auto-open feature to release heat, and after a while, the dishes dry. I didn't have to dry them every time I washed them by hand. And this product has a stainless steel top, so I don't have to worry. This was a big plus, and it played a part in my decision. So, I bought it to reduce the time I spend doing housework, such as washing dishes. I've been using it and it's great because I can do other things during the dishwashing time or take a break when I'm tired. Comments (English): My money, my country / Media 6-person dishwasher review. Product basic information. Media 6-person dishwasher with automatic door opening and UV lamp. Color: White, Model name: (MDWMT0601W-WIN-KR). Window design. Free A/S period. 2-year free repairs available through Coupang Customer Service. Friendly and fast delivery. I paid with Coupang Rocket Delivery, and the technician came and installed it the next day, Sunday. I was satisfied with the fast delivery and installation in one day, and the technician was very friendly. Window design. I was originally considering the basic design of the Media dishwasher, but I ultimately decided on the window type. The reason was that it had a more open feel, a prettier design, and an added UV sterilization function. The price difference was only about 40,000 won compared to the basic design model. I decided to go with this one because I thought I would use it for a long time once I bought it, and after discussing it with my husband, I decided. Reasonable price. It turned out that various large companies were selling dishwashers manufactured by Media. They were selling them at a higher price with slightly different labels and designs. Knowing that, I wondered if it was really necessary to buy it at a higher price. So I searched for media and found out that Coupang officially imported it and provided 2 years of free A/S, so I bought it. When I tried running the low-noise dishwasher, it was quieter than I thought. Honestly, I was surprised by how quiet it was. Since it's the type that you use on top of the sink, I expected it to be quite noisy. By my standards, it's really quiet. It's perfect for a house with a baby. Cleaning power + convenience. The decisive reason I bought the dishwasher was because I'm seven months pregnant, and now I can't stand still without any pain in my back, hips, stomach, or knees due to the weight of my belly. So, I bought it to reduce the time I spend doing housework, such as washing dishes. I've been using it and it's great because I can do other things during the dishwashing time or take a break when I'm tired. Also, we'll be a family of three soon after the baby is born, and since we mostly eat home-cooked meals rather than eating out, I could see how much better my quality of life would be if the dishwasher cleaned the dishes and bottles more thoroughly than I could. I used it and was very satisfied with the automatic door opening function because I didn't have to wait for the dishwasher to finish and then manually open the door. The glass cups looked even clearer than the ones I washed myself! I cleaned the dishes thoroughly, top, middle, and bottom, three times, so if you play Tetris well, there's no place that's not cleaned. I searched on Coupang and bought some eco-friendly liquid detergent in advance and poured it in. The latest version of Jayeonpong dishwasher-specific liquid detergent has good reviews for its three-fold enhanced cleaning power, in addition to regular dishes. It has a lemony scent that leaves no residue, and it smells good. It's also reasonably priced, so I plan to continue using it. The only downside is that this model doesn't have hot air drying. But since most six-person dishwashers do, I understand and can overlook it. The dishwasher intelligently uses the auto-open feature to release heat, and after a while, the dishes dry. I didn't have to dry them every time I washed them by hand. And this product has a stainless steel top, so I don't have to worry. This was a big plus, and it played a part in my decision. This is my honest review of a product I purchased with my own money. If it helped you make a purchase, please let me know. Please press and hold! To improve your quality of life, I highly recommend the Media Dishwasher!

Comments (English): [ I am extremely satisfied with the express installation and delivery within just one day of purchase. ] || ---------------- || Reason for purchase (I'm being completely honest, I bought this with my own money). Dishwashers are a must-have item for everyone these days; those who haven't used one might not know, but for those who have, it's a whole new world. So, to make life a little easier, I brought in a "dishwasher lady." Since I bought it with my own money, I wanted to be careful. I debated between the 8-place, 12-place, and 14-place models available on the market. However, given my personality—I can't stand seeing dishes pile up—I'd rather run it one more time than do it all at once. (I'm such a fuss!) I settled on the 6-place model. I watched YouTube and Naver blogs, and I spent two whole days researching before making a decision. Although Coupang offers a 2-year warranty, it was honestly an unfamiliar brand to me. To be cautious, I looked up a lot of reviews before buying. I looked at L, Sam, Coupang, Mi, S... and I decided on this one. Someone once told me that as long as the dishwashing function works well, the brand doesn't really matter. So, I decided on a product that is a bit cheaper but offers great value for money. Advantages of the Midea Dishwasher: 1. It has a 2-tier rack inside that separates, allowing large pots and bulky dishes to fit inside. 2. Its compact size allows for installation even in narrow spaces. 3. It can be installed in the kitchen without drilling holes. 4. It adds a great touch to your interior decor. 5. It saves water. Based on my criteria, I hesitated a lot because it doesn't have UV sterilization or hot air drying. While UV sterilization is nice to have, I didn't find it that great when I used a baby bottle sterilizer. Also, since my baby is currently 6 years old, I felt it wouldn't be necessary, so I passed on it. People said the hot air drying feature is a game changer and is great to have, but opinions are divided, so I passed on that too. I saw reviews saying it's basically drying with a folding dryer. It has an automatic door opening function, so I passed on that as well. If I were to weigh every single factor and buy one that perfectly suits my taste, there would be no end to the choices and the price would go up. I had a benchmark of exactly around the 400,000 won mark. That is why I chose it. It has automatic door opening and allows you to put items in the middle, so... well, it's better than washing dishes by hand. I set the price at 400,000 won and got drill-free installation, so I'm very satisfied in my own way. For those of you considering a dishwasher, I recommend getting one right away. I used to think, "It would be convenient to have, but how much convenience could I really make?" But it is definitely convenient and cleans thoroughly. I think all dishwashers are pretty much the same. I am a family of three who cooks all our meals at home; it is sufficient for one baby and two adults. I hope my review is helpful~~~. Additional review after Day 1 use: The basic function takes about 75 minutes. You cannot use plastic food container lids (the rubber ones). The cutlery holder is a bit small, but it fits perfectly with my baby's (6-year-old) spoons and forks. For the adults, I just put them inside the dishwasher and ran it. When I removed the top tray, a large wok fits in. Hmm. Also, I was surprised by how much fits in it, much more than I expected. Hot air drying? I heard it was good to have that feature, so I agonized over it for a while before finally buying this one. Even on the basic 75-minute dishwashing function, the door opens automatically. There is a little moisture, but I just wiped it lightly with a dry dishcloth or paper towel. If it’s not urgent, I think it will dry pretty well if I just leave the door a little open. Having never used one before, this is a whole new world. I saw an LG washing machine at another house today, and it wasn't anything special. I heard you only need to do a drum wash about once a month, so I bought a Pringles and plan to do that. I agonized over buying it, but it really is a whole new world that I bought with my own money. Should I say I have more time? For those of you who are debating, the 6-person capacity is sufficient for a family of three. If you gather all the dishes from the day in one go in the evening, it’s enough. Oh! For those wondering about the noise... it’s not unpleasant; it’s about the sound of water filling up in a washing machine. It’s quieter than a vacuum cleaner, quieter than inter-floor noise, and quieter than a baby crying. It’s just about the same level as the water coming out when you’re washing dishes. I'm satisfied. My aunt is the best!

So, to make life a little easier, I brought in a "dishwasher lady." Since I bought it with my own money, I wanted to be careful. I debated between the 8-place, 12-place, and 14-place models available on the market. However, given my personality—I can't stand seeing dishes pile up—I'd rather run it one more time than do it all at once. (I'm such a fuss!) I settled on the 6-place model. I watched YouTube and Naver blogs, and I spent two whole days researching before making a decision. Although Coupang offers a 2-year warranty, it was honestly an unfamiliar brand to me. To be cautious, I looked up a lot of reviews before buying. I looked at L, Sam, Coupang, Mi, S... and I decided on this one. Someone once told me that as long as the dishwashing function works well, the brand doesn't really matter. So, I decided on a product that is a bit cheaper but offers great value for money. Advantages of the Midea Dishwasher: 1. It has a 2-tier rack inside that separates, allowing large pots and bulky dishes to fit inside. 2. Its compact size allows for installation even in narrow spaces. 3. It can be installed in the kitchen without drilling holes. 4. It adds a great touch to your interior decor. 5. It saves water. Based on my criteria, I hesitated a lot because it doesn't have UV sterilization or hot air drying. While UV sterilization is nice to have, I didn't find it that great when I used a baby bottle sterilizer. Also, since my baby is currently 6 years old, I felt it wouldn't be necessary, so I passed on it. People said the hot air drying feature is a game changer and is great to have, but opinions are divided, so I passed on that too. I saw reviews saying it's basically drying with a folding dryer. It has an automatic door opening function, so I passed on that as well. If I were to weigh every single factor and buy one that perfectly suits my taste, there would be no end to the choices and the price would go up. I had a benchmark of exactly around the 400,000 won mark. That is why I chose it. It has automatic door opening and allows you to put items in the middle, so... well, it's better than washing dishes by hand. I set the price at 400,000 won and got drill-free installation, so I'm very satisfied in my own way. For those of you considering a dishwasher, I recommend getting one right away. I used to think, "It would be convenient to have, but how much convenience could I really make?" But it is definitely convenient and cleans thoroughly. I think all dishwashers are pretty much the same. I am a family of three who cooks all our meals at home; it is sufficient for one baby and two adults. I hope my review is helpful~~~. Additional review after Day 1 use: The basic function takes about 75 minutes. You cannot use plastic food container lids (the rubber ones). The cutlery holder is a bit small, but it fits perfectly with my baby's (6-year-old) spoons and forks. For the adults, I just put them inside the dishwasher and ran it. When I removed the top tray, a large wok fits in. Hmm. Also, I was surprised by how much fits in it, much more than I expected. Hot air drying? I heard it was good to have that feature, so I agonized over it for a while before finally buying this one. Even on the basic 75-minute dishwashing function, the door opens automatically. There is a little moisture, but I just wiped it lightly with a dry dishcloth or paper towel. If it’s not urgent, I think it will dry pretty well if I just leave the door a little open. Having never used one before, this is a whole new world. I saw an LG washing machine at another house today, and it wasn't anything special. I heard you only need to do a drum wash about once a month, so I bought a Pringles and plan to do that. I agonized over buying it, but it really is a whole new world that I bought with my own money. Should I say I have more time? For those of you who are debating, the 6-person capacity is sufficient for a family of three. If you gather all the dishes from the day in one go in the evening, it’s enough. Oh! For those wondering about the noise... it’s not unpleasant; it’s about the sound of water filling up in a washing machine. It’s quieter than a vacuum cleaner, quieter than inter-floor noise, and quieter than a baby crying. It’s just about the same level as the water coming out when you’re washing dishes. I'm satisfied. My aunt is the best!

Dishwashers are a must-have item for everyone these days; those who haven't used one might not know, but for those who have, it's a whole new world. So, to make life a little easier, I brought in a "dishwasher lady." Since I bought it with my own money, I wanted to be careful. I debated between the 8-place, 12-place, and 14-place models available on the market. However, given my personality—I can't stand seeing dishes pile up—I'd rather run it one more time than do it all at once. (I'm such a fuss!) I settled on the 6-place model. I watched YouTube and Naver blogs, and I spent two whole days researching before making a decision. Although Coupang offers a 2-year warranty, it was honestly an unfamiliar brand to me. To be cautious, I looked up a lot of reviews before buying. I looked at L, Sam, Coupang, Mi, S... and I decided on this one. Someone once told me that as long as the dishwashing function works well, the brand doesn't really matter. So, I decided on a product that is a bit cheaper but offers great value for money. Advantages of the Midea Dishwasher: 1. It has a 2-tier rack inside that separates, allowing large pots and bulky dishes to fit inside. 2. Its compact size allows for installation even in narrow spaces. 3. It can be installed in the kitchen without drilling holes. 4. It adds a great touch to your interior decor. 5. It saves water. Based on my criteria, I hesitated a lot because it doesn't have UV sterilization or hot air drying. While UV sterilization is nice to have, I didn't find it that great when I used a baby bottle sterilizer. Also, since my baby is currently 6 years old, I felt it wouldn't be necessary, so I passed on it. People said the hot air drying feature is a game changer and is great to have, but opinions are divided, so I passed on that too. I saw reviews saying it's basically drying with a folding dryer. It has an automatic door opening function, so I passed on that as well. If I were to weigh every single factor and buy one that perfectly suits my taste, there would be no end to the choices and the price would go up. I had a benchmark of exactly around the 400,000 won mark. That is why I chose it. It has automatic door opening and allows you to put items in the middle, so... well, it's better than washing dishes by hand. I set the price at 400,000 won and got drill-free installation, so I'm very satisfied in my own way. For those of you considering a dishwasher, I recommend getting one right away. I used to think, "It would be convenient to have, but how much convenience could I really make?" But it is definitely convenient and cleans thoroughly. I think all dishwashers are pretty much the same. I am a family of three who cooks all our meals at home; it is sufficient for one baby and two adults. I hope my review is helpful~~~. Additional review after Day 1 use: The basic function takes about 75 minutes. You cannot use plastic food container lids (the rubber ones). The cutlery holder is a bit small, but it fits perfectly with my baby's (6-year-old) spoons and forks. For the adults, I just put them inside the dishwasher and ran it. When I removed the top tray, a large wok fits in. Hmm. Also, I was surprised by how much fits in it, much more than I expected. Hot air drying? I heard it was good to have that feature, so I agonized over it for a while before finally buying this one. Even on the basic 75-minute dishwashing function, the door opens automatically. There is a little moisture, but I just wiped it lightly with a dry dishcloth or paper towel. If it’s not urgent, I think it will dry pretty well if I just leave the door a little open. Having never used one before, this is a whole new world. I saw an LG washing machine at another house today, and it wasn't anything special. I heard you only need to do a drum wash about once a month, so I bought a Pringles and plan to do that. I agonized over buying it, but it really is a whole new world that I bought with my own money. Should I say I have more time? For those of you who are debating, the 6-person capacity is sufficient for a family of three. If you gather all the dishes from the day in one go in the evening, it’s enough. Oh! For those wondering about the noise... it’s not unpleasant; it’s about the sound of water filling up in a washing machine. It’s quieter than a vacuum cleaner, quieter than inter-floor noise, and quieter than a baby crying. It’s just about the same level as the water coming out when you’re washing dishes. I'm satisfied. My aunt is the best!

Additional review after Day 1 use: The basic function takes about 75 minutes. You cannot use plastic food container lids (the rubber ones). The cutlery holder is a bit small, but it fits perfectly with my baby's (6-year-old) spoons and forks. For the adults, I just put them inside the dishwasher and ran it. When I removed the top tray, a large wok fits in. Hmm. Also, I was surprised by how much fits in it, much more than I expected. Hot air drying? I heard it was good to have that feature, so I agonized over it for a while before finally buying this one. Even on the basic 75-minute dishwashing function, the door opens automatically. There is a little moisture, but I just wiped it lightly with a dry dishcloth or paper towel. If it’s not urgent, I think it will dry pretty well if I just leave the door a little open. Having never used one before, this is a whole new world. I saw an LG washing machine at another house today, and it wasn't anything special. I heard you only need to do a drum wash about once a month, so I bought a Pringles and plan to do that. I agonized over buying it, but it really is a whole new world that I bought with my own money. Should I say I have more time? For those of you who are debating, the 6-person capacity is sufficient for a family of three. If you gather all the dishes from the day in one go in the evening, it’s enough. Oh! For those wondering about the noise... it’s not unpleasant; it’s about the sound of water filling up in a washing machine. It’s quieter than a vacuum cleaner, quieter than inter-floor noise, and quieter than a baby crying. It’s just about the same level as the water coming out when you’re washing dishes. I'm satisfied. My aunt is the best!

So, to make life a little easier, I brought in a "dishwasher lady." Since I bought it with my own money, I wanted to be careful. I debated between the 8-place, 12-place, and 14-place models available on the market. However, given my personality—I can't stand seeing dishes pile up—I'd rather run it one more time than do it all at once. (I'm such a fuss!) I settled on the 6-place model. I watched YouTube and Naver blogs, and I spent two whole days researching before making a decision. Although Coupang offers a 2-year warranty, it was honestly an unfamiliar brand to me. To be cautious, I looked up a lot of reviews before buying. I looked at L, Sam, Coupang, Mi, S... and I decided on this one. Someone once told me that as long as the dishwashing function works well, the brand doesn't really matter. So, I decided on a product that is a bit cheaper but offers great value for money. Advantages of the Midea Dishwasher: 1. It has a 2-tier rack inside that separates, allowing large pots and bulky dishes to fit inside. 2. Its compact size allows for installation even in narrow spaces. 3. It can be installed in the kitchen without drilling holes. 4. It adds a great touch to your interior decor. 5. It saves water. Based on my criteria, I hesitated a lot because it doesn't have UV sterilization or hot air drying. While UV sterilization is nice to have, I didn't find it that great when I used a baby bottle sterilizer. Also, since my baby is currently 6 years old, I felt it wouldn't be necessary, so I passed on it. People said the hot air drying feature is a game changer and is great to have, but opinions are divided, so I passed on that too. I saw reviews saying it's basically drying with a folding dryer. It has an automatic door opening function, so I passed on that as well. If I were to weigh every single factor and buy one that perfectly suits my taste, there would be no end to the choices and the price would go up. I had a benchmark of exactly around the 400,000 won mark. That is why I chose it. It has automatic door opening and allows you to put items in the middle, so... well, it's better than washing dishes by hand. I set the price at 400,000 won and got drill-free installation, so I'm very satisfied in my own way. For those of you considering a dishwasher, I recommend getting one right away. I used to think, "It would be convenient to have, but how much convenience could I really make?" But it is definitely convenient and cleans thoroughly. I think all dishwashers are pretty much the same. I am a family of three who cooks all our meals at home; it is sufficient for one baby and two adults. I hope my review is helpful~~~. Additional review after Day 1 use: The basic function takes about 75 minutes. You cannot use plastic food container lids (the rubber ones). The cutlery holder is a bit small, but it fits perfectly with my baby's (6-year-old) spoons and forks. For the adults, I just put them inside the dishwasher and ran it. When I removed the top tray, a large wok fits in. Hmm. Also, I was surprised by how much fits in it, much more than I expected. Hot air drying? I heard it was good to have that feature, so I agonized over it for a while before finally buying this one. Even on the basic 75-minute dishwashing function, the door opens automatically. There is a little moisture, but I just wiped it lightly with a dry dishcloth or paper towel. If it’s not urgent, I think it will dry pretty well if I just leave the door a little open. Having never used one before, this is a whole new world. I saw an LG washing machine at another house today, and it wasn't anything special. I heard you only need to do a drum wash about once a month, so I bought a Pringles and plan to do that. I agonized over buying it, but it really is a whole new world that I bought with my own money. Should I say I have more time? For those of you who are debating, the 6-person capacity is sufficient for a family of three. If you gather all the dishes from the day in one go in the evening, it’s enough. Oh! For those wondering about the noise... it’s not unpleasant; it’s about the sound of water filling up in a washing machine. It’s quieter than a vacuum cleaner, quieter than inter-floor noise, and quieter than a baby crying. It’s just about the same level as the water coming out when you’re washing dishes. I'm satisfied. My aunt is the best!

I debated between the 8-place, 12-place, and 14-place models available on the market. However, given my personality—I can't stand seeing dishes pile up—I'd rather run it one more time than do it all at once. (I'm such a fuss!) I settled on the 6-place model. I watched YouTube and Naver blogs, and I spent two whole days researching before making a decision. Although Coupang offers a 2-year warranty, it was honestly an unfamiliar brand to me. To be cautious, I looked up a lot of reviews before buying. I looked at L, Sam, Coupang, Mi, S... and I decided on this one. Someone once told me that as long as the dishwashing function works well, the brand doesn't really matter. So, I decided on a product that is a bit cheaper but offers great value for money. Based on my criteria, I hesitated a lot because it doesn't have UV sterilization or hot air drying. While UV sterilization is nice to have, I didn't find it that great when I used a baby bottle sterilizer. Also, since my baby is currently 6 years old, I felt it wouldn't be necessary, so I passed on it. It has an automatic door opening function, so I passed on that as well. If I were to weigh every single factor and buy one that perfectly suits my taste, there would be no end to the choices and the price would go up. I had a benchmark of exactly around the 400,000 won mark. That is why I chose it. I set the price at 400,000 won and got drill-free installation, so I'm very satisfied in my own way. For those of you considering a dishwasher, I recommend getting one right away. I used to think, "It would be convenient to have, but how much convenience could I really make?" But it is definitely convenient and cleans thoroughly. I think all dishwashers are pretty much the same. I am a family of three who cooks all our meals at home; it is sufficient for one baby and two adults. I hope my review is helpful~~~. Additional review after Day 1 use: The basic function takes about 75 minutes. You cannot use plastic food container lids (the rubber ones). The cutlery holder is a bit small, but it fits perfectly with my baby's (6-year-old) spoons and forks. For the adults, I just put them inside the dishwasher and ran it. When I removed the top tray, a large wok fits in. Hmm. Also, I was surprised by how much fits in it, much more than I expected. Hot air drying? I heard it was good to have that feature, so I agonized over it for a while before finally buying this one. Even on the basic 75-minute dishwashing function, the door opens automatically. There is a little moisture, but I just wiped it lightly with a dry dishcloth or paper towel. If it’s not urgent, I think it will dry pretty well if I just leave the door a little open. Having never used one before, this is a whole new world. I saw an LG washing machine at another house today, and it wasn't anything special. I heard you only need to do a drum wash about once a month, so I bought a Pringles and plan to do that. I agonized over buying it, but it really is a whole new world that I bought with my own money. Should I say I have more time? For those of you who are debating, the 6-person capacity is sufficient for a family of three. If you gather all the dishes from the day in one go in the evening, it’s enough. Oh! For those wondering about the noise... it’s not unpleasant; it’s about the sound of water filling up in a washing machine. It’s quieter than a vacuum cleaner, quieter than inter-floor noise, and quieter than a baby crying. It’s just about the same level as the water coming out when you’re washing dishes. I'm satisfied. My aunt is the best!

Dishwashers are a must-have item for everyone these days; those who haven't used one might not know, but for those who have, it's a whole new world. So, to make life a little easier, I brought in a "dishwasher lady." Since I bought it with my own money, I wanted to be careful. I debated between the 8-place, 12-place, and 14-place models available on the market. However, given my personality—I can't stand seeing dishes pile up—I'd rather run it one more time than do it all at once. (I'm such a fuss!) I settled on the 6-place model. I watched YouTube and Naver blogs, and I spent two whole days researching before making a decision. Although Coupang offers a 2-year warranty, it was honestly an unfamiliar brand to me. To be cautious, I looked up a lot of reviews before buying. I looked at L, Sam, Coupang, Mi, S... and I decided on this one. Someone once told me that as long as the dishwashing function works well, the brand doesn't really matter. So, I decided on a product that is a bit cheaper but offers great value for money. Advantages of the Midea Dishwasher: 1. It has a 2-tier rack inside that separates, allowing large pots and bulky dishes to fit inside. 2. Its compact size allows for installation even in narrow spaces. 3. It can be installed in the kitchen without drilling holes. 4. It adds a great touch to your interior decor. 5. It saves water. Based on my criteria, I hesitated a lot because it doesn't have UV sterilization or hot air drying. While UV sterilization is nice to have, I didn't find it that great when I used a baby bottle sterilizer. Also, since my baby is currently 6 years old, I felt it wouldn't be necessary, so I passed on it. People said the hot air drying feature is a game changer and is great to have, but opinions are divided, so I passed on that too. I saw reviews saying it's basically drying with a folding dryer. It has an automatic door opening function, so I passed on that as well. If I were to weigh every single factor and buy one that perfectly suits my taste, there would be no end to the choices and the price would go up. I had a benchmark of exactly around the 400,000 won mark. That is why I chose it. It has automatic door opening and allows you to put items in the middle, so... well, it's better than washing dishes by hand. I set the price at 400,000 won and got drill-free installation, so I'm very satisfied in my own way. For those of you considering a dishwasher, I recommend getting one right away. I used to think, "It would be convenient to have, but how much convenience could I really make?" But it is definitely convenient and cleans thoroughly. I think all dishwashers are pretty much the same. I am a family of three who cooks all our meals at home; it is sufficient for one baby and two adults. I hope my review is helpful~~~. Additional review after Day 1 use: The basic function takes about 75 minutes. You cannot use plastic food container lids (the rubber ones). The cutlery holder is a bit small, but it fits perfectly with my baby's (6-year-old) spoons and forks. For the adults, I just put them inside the dishwasher and ran it. When I removed the top tray, a large wok fits in. Hmm. Also, I was surprised by how much fits in it, much more than I expected. Hot air drying? I heard it was good to have that feature, so I agonized over it for a while before finally buying this one. Even on the basic 75-minute dishwashing function, the door opens automatically. There is a little moisture, but I just wiped it lightly with a dry dishcloth or paper towel. If it’s not urgent, I think it will dry pretty well if I just leave the door a little open. Having never used one before, this is a whole new world. I saw an LG washing machine at another house today, and it wasn't anything special. I heard you only need to do a drum wash about once a month, so I bought a Pringles and plan to do that. I agonized over buying it, but it really is a whole new world that I bought with my own money. Should I say I have more time? For those of you who are debating, the 6-person capacity is sufficient for a family of three. If you gather all the dishes from the day in one go in the evening, it’s enough. Oh! For those wondering about the noise... it’s not unpleasant; it’s about the sound of water filling up in a washing machine. It’s quieter than a vacuum cleaner, quieter than inter-floor noise, and quieter than a baby crying. It’s just about the same level as the water coming out when you’re washing dishes. I'm satisfied. My aunt is the best!

Comments (English): [ I am extremely satisfied with the express installation and delivery within just one day of purchase. ] || ---------------- || Reason for purchase (I'm being completely honest, I bought this with my own money). Dishwashers are a must-have item for everyone these days; those who haven't used one might not know, but for those who have, it's a whole new world. So, to make life a little easier, I brought in a "dishwasher lady." Since I bought it with my own money, I wanted to be careful. I debated between the 8-place, 12-place, and 14-place models available on the market. However, given my personality—I can't stand seeing dishes pile up—I'd rather run it one more time than do it all at once. (I'm such a fuss!) I settled on the 6-place model. I watched YouTube and Naver blogs, and I spent two whole days researching before making a decision. Although Coupang offers a 2-year warranty, it was honestly an unfamiliar brand to me. To be cautious, I looked up a lot of reviews before buying. I looked at L, Sam, Coupang, Mi, S... and I decided on this one. Someone once told me that as long as the dishwashing function works well, the brand doesn't really matter. So, I decided on a product that is a bit cheaper but offers great value for money. Advantages of the Midea Dishwasher: 1. It has a 2-tier rack inside that separates, allowing large pots and bulky dishes to fit inside. 2. Its compact size allows for installation even in narrow spaces. 3. It can be installed in the kitchen without drilling holes. 4. It adds a great touch to your interior decor. 5. It saves water. Based on my criteria, I hesitated a lot because it doesn't have UV sterilization or hot air drying. While UV sterilization is nice to have, I didn't find it that great when I used a baby bottle sterilizer. Also, since my baby is currently 6 years old, I felt it wouldn't be necessary, so I passed on it. People said the hot air drying feature is a game changer and is great to have, but opinions are divided, so I passed on that too. I saw reviews saying it's basically drying with a folding dryer. It has an automatic door opening function, so I passed on that as well. If I were to weigh every single factor and buy one that perfectly suits my taste, there would be no end to the choices and the price would go up. I had a benchmark of exactly around the 400,000 won mark. That is why I chose it. It has automatic door opening and allows you to put items in the middle, so... well, it's better than washing dishes by hand. I set the price at 400,000 won and got drill-free installation, so I'm very satisfied in my own way. For those of you considering a dishwasher, I recommend getting one right away. I used to think, "It would be convenient to have, but how much convenience could I really make?" But it is definitely convenient and cleans thoroughly. I think all dishwashers are pretty much the same. I am a family of three who cooks all our meals at home; it is sufficient for one baby and two adults. I hope my review is helpful~~~. Additional review after Day 1 use: The basic function takes about 75 minutes. You cannot use plastic food container lids (the rubber ones). The cutlery holder is a bit small, but it fits perfectly with my baby's (6-year-old) spoons and forks. For the adults, I just put them inside the dishwasher and ran it. When I removed the top tray, a large wok fits in. Hmm. Also, I was surprised by how much fits in it, much more than I expected. Hot air drying? I heard it was good to have that feature, so I agonized over it for a while before finally buying this one. Even on the basic 75-minute dishwashing function, the door opens automatically. There is a little moisture, but I just wiped it lightly with a dry dishcloth or paper towel. If it’s not urgent, I think it will dry pretty well if I just leave the door a little open. Having never used one before, this is a whole new world. I saw an LG washing machine at another house today, and it wasn't anything special. I heard you only need to do a drum wash about once a month, so I bought a Pringles and plan to do that. I agonized over buying it, but it really is a whole new world that I bought with my own money. Should I say I have more time? For those of you who are debating, the 6-person capacity is sufficient for a family of three. If you gather all the dishes from the day in one go in the evening, it’s enough. Oh! For those wondering about the noise... it’s not unpleasant; it’s about the sound of water filling up in a washing machine. It’s quieter than a vacuum cleaner, quieter than inter-floor noise, and quieter than a baby crying. It’s just about the same level as the water coming out when you’re washing dishes. I'm satisfied. My aunt is the best!

Additional review after Day 1 use: The basic function takes about 75 minutes. You cannot use plastic food container lids (the rubber ones). The cutlery holder is a bit small, but it fits perfectly with my baby's (6-year-old) spoons and forks. For the adults, I just put them inside the dishwasher and ran it. When I removed the top tray, a large wok fits in. Hmm. Also, I was surprised by how much fits in it, much more than I expected. Hot air drying? I heard it was good to have that feature, so I agonized over it for a while before finally buying this one. Even on the basic 75-minute dishwashing function, the door opens automatically. There is a little moisture, but I just wiped it lightly with a dry dishcloth or paper towel. If it’s not urgent, I think it will dry pretty well if I just leave the door a little open. Having never used one before, this is a whole new world. I saw an LG washing machine at another house today, and it wasn't anything special. I heard you only need to do a drum wash about once a month, so I bought a Pringles and plan to do that. I agonized over buying it, but it really is a whole new world that I bought with my own money. Should I say I have more time? For those of you who are debating, the 6-person capacity is sufficient for a family of three. If you gather all the dishes from the day in one go in the evening, it’s enough. Oh! For those wondering about the noise... it’s not unpleasant; it’s about the sound of water filling up in a washing machine. It’s quieter than a vacuum cleaner, quieter than inter-floor noise, and quieter than a baby crying. It’s just about the same level as the water coming out when you’re washing dishes. I'm satisfied. My aunt is the best!

Additional review after Day 1 use: The basic function takes about 75 minutes. You cannot use plastic food container lids (the rubber ones). The cutlery holder is a bit small, but it fits perfectly with my baby's (6-year-old) spoons and forks. For the adults, I just put them inside the dishwasher and ran it. When I removed the top tray, a large wok fits in. Hmm. Also, I was surprised by how much fits in it, much more than I expected. Hot air drying? I heard it was good to have that feature, so I agonized over it for a while before finally buying this one. Even on the basic 75-minute dishwashing function, the door opens automatically. There is a little moisture, but I just wiped it lightly with a dry dishcloth or paper towel. If it’s not urgent, I think it will dry pretty well if I just leave the door a little open. Having never used one before, this is a whole new world. I saw an LG washing machine at another house today, and it wasn't anything special. I heard you only need to do a drum wash about once a month, so I bought a Pringles and plan to do that. I agonized over buying it, but it really is a whole new world that I bought with my own money. Should I say I have more time? For those of you who are debating, the 6-person capacity is sufficient for a family of three. If you gather all the dishes from the day in one go in the evening, it’s enough. Oh! For those wondering about the noise... it’s not unpleasant; it’s about the sound of water filling up in a washing machine. It’s quieter than a vacuum cleaner, quieter than inter-floor noise, and quieter than a baby crying. It’s just about the same level as the water coming out when you’re washing dishes. I'm satisfied. My aunt is the best!

So, to make life a little easier, I brought in a "dishwasher lady." Since I bought it with my own money, I wanted to be careful. I debated between the 8-place, 12-place, and 14-place models available on the market. However, given my personality—I can't stand seeing dishes pile up—I'd rather run it one more time than do it all at once. (I'm such a fuss!) I settled on the 6-place model. I watched YouTube and Naver blogs, and I spent two whole days researching before making a decision. Although Coupang offers a 2-year warranty, it was honestly an unfamiliar brand to me. To be cautious, I looked up a lot of reviews before buying. I looked at L, Sam, Coupang, Mi, S... and I decided on this one. Someone once told me that as long as the dishwashing function works well, the brand doesn't really matter. So, I decided on a product that is a bit cheaper but offers great value for money. Its compact size allows for installation even in narrow spaces. 3. It can be installed in the kitchen without drilling holes. 4. It adds a great touch to your interior decor. 5. It saves water. Based on my criteria, I hesitated a lot because it doesn't have UV sterilization or hot air drying. While UV sterilization is nice to have, I didn't find it that great when I used a baby bottle sterilizer. Also, since my baby is currently 6 years old, I felt it wouldn't be necessary, so I passed on it. People said the hot air drying feature is a game changer and is great to have, but opinions are divided, so I passed on that too. I saw reviews saying it's basically drying with a folding dryer. It has an automatic door opening function, so I passed on that as well. If I were to weigh every single factor and buy one that perfectly suits my taste, there would be no end to the choices and the price would go up. I had a benchmark of exactly around the 400,000 won mark. That is why I chose it. It has automatic door opening and allows you to put items in the middle, so... well, it's better than washing dishes by hand. I set the price at 400,000 won and got drill-free installation, so I'm very satisfied in my own way. For those of you considering a dishwasher, I recommend getting one right away. I used to think, "It would be convenient to have, but how much convenience could I really make?" But it is definitely convenient and cleans thoroughly. I think all dishwashers are pretty much the same. I am a family of three who cooks all our meals at home; it is sufficient for one baby and two adults. I hope my review is helpful~~~. Additional review after Day 1 use: The basic function takes about 75 minutes. You cannot use plastic food container lids (the rubber ones). The cutlery holder is a bit small, but it fits perfectly with my baby's (6-year-old) spoons and forks. For the adults, I just put them inside the dishwasher and ran it. When I removed the top tray, a large wok fits in. Hmm. Also, I was surprised by how much fits in it, much more than I expected. Hot air drying? I heard it was good to have that feature, so I agonized over it for a while before finally buying this one. Even on the basic 75-minute dishwashing function, the door opens automatically. There is a little moisture, but I just wiped it lightly with a dry dishcloth or paper towel. If it’s not urgent, I think it will dry pretty well if I just leave the door a little open. Having never used one before, this is a whole new world. I saw an LG washing machine at another house today, and it wasn't anything special. I heard you only need to do a drum wash about once a month, so I bought a Pringles and plan to do that. I agonized over buying it, but it really is a whole new world that I bought with my own money. Should I say I have more time? For those of you who are debating, the 6-person capacity is sufficient for a family of three. If you gather all the dishes from the day in one go in the evening, it’s enough. Oh! For those wondering about the noise... it’s not unpleasant; it’s about the sound of water filling up in a washing machine. It’s quieter than a vacuum cleaner, quieter than inter-floor noise, and quieter than a baby crying. It’s just about the same level as the water coming out when you’re washing dishes. I'm satisfied. My aunt is the best!

Additional review after Day 1 use: The basic function takes about 75 minutes. You cannot use plastic food container lids (the rubber ones). The cutlery holder is a bit small, but it fits perfectly with my baby's (6-year-old) spoons and forks. For the adults, I just put them inside the dishwasher and ran it. When I removed the top tray, a large wok fits in. Hmm. Also, I was surprised by how much fits in it, much more than I expected. Hot air drying? I heard it was good to have that feature, so I agonized over it for a while before finally buying this one. Even on the basic 75-minute dishwashing function, the door opens automatically. There is a little moisture, but I just wiped it lightly with a dry dishcloth or paper towel. If it’s not urgent, I think it will dry pretty well if I just leave the door a little open. Having never used one before, this is a whole new world. I saw an LG washing machine at another house today, and it wasn't anything special. I heard you only need to do a drum wash about once a month, so I bought a Pringles and plan to do that. I agonized over buying it, but it really is a whole new world that I bought with my own money. Should I say I have more time? For those of you who are debating, the 6-person capacity is sufficient for a family of three. If you gather all the dishes from the day in one go in the evening, it’s enough. Oh! For those wondering about the noise... it’s not unpleasant; it’s about the sound of water filling up in a washing machine. It’s quieter than a vacuum cleaner, quieter than inter-floor noise, and quieter than a baby crying. It’s just about the same level as the water coming out when you’re washing dishes. I'm satisfied. My aunt is the best!

Additional review after Day 1 use: The basic function takes about 75 minutes. You cannot use plastic food container lids (the rubber ones). The cutlery holder is a bit small, but it fits perfectly with my baby's (6-year-old) spoons and forks. For the adults, I just put them inside the dishwasher and ran it. When I removed the top tray, a large wok fits in. Hmm. Also, I was surprised by how much fits in it, much more than I expected. Hot air drying? I heard it was good to have that feature, so I agonized over it for a while before finally buying this one. Even on the basic 75-minute dishwashing function, the door opens automatically. There is a little moisture, but I just wiped it lightly with a dry dishcloth or paper towel. If it’s not urgent, I think it will dry pretty well if I just leave the door a little open. Having never used one before, this is a whole new world. I saw an LG washing machine at another house today, and it wasn't anything special. I heard you only need to do a drum wash about once a month, so I bought a Pringles and plan to do that. I agonized over buying it, but it really is a whole new world that I bought with my own money. Should I say I have more time? For those of you who are debating, the 6-person capacity is sufficient for a family of three. If you gather all the dishes from the day in one go in the evening, it’s enough. Oh! For those wondering about the noise... it’s not unpleasant; it’s about the sound of water filling up in a washing machine. It’s quieter than a vacuum cleaner, quieter than inter-floor noise, and quieter than a baby crying. It’s just about the same level as the water coming out when you’re washing dishes. I'm satisfied. My aunt is the best!

I debated between the 8-place, 12-place, and 14-place models available on the market. I watched YouTube and Naver blogs, and I spent two whole days researching before making a decision. Although Coupang offers a 2-year warranty, it was honestly an unfamiliar brand to me. To be cautious, I looked up a lot of reviews before buying. I looked at L, Sam, Coupang, Mi, S... and I decided on this one. Someone once told me that as long as the dishwashing function works well, the brand doesn't really matter. So, I decided on a product that is a bit cheaper but offers great value for money. Based on my criteria, I hesitated a lot because it doesn't have UV sterilization or hot air drying. While UV sterilization is nice to have, I didn't find it that great when I used a baby bottle sterilizer. Also, since my baby is currently 6 years old, I felt it wouldn't be necessary, so I passed on it. It has an automatic door opening function, so I passed on that as well. If I were to weigh every single factor and buy one that perfectly suits my taste, there would be no end to the choices and the price would go up. I had a benchmark of exactly around the 400,000 won mark. That is why I chose it. I set the price at 400,000 won and got drill-free installation, so I'm very satisfied in my own way. For those of you considering a dishwasher, I recommend getting one right away. I used to think, "It would be convenient to have, but how much convenience could I really make?" But it is definitely convenient and cleans thoroughly. I think all dishwashers are pretty much the same. I am a family of three who cooks all our meals at home; it is sufficient for one baby and two adults. I hope my review is helpful~~~. Additional review after Day 1 use: The basic function takes about 75 minutes. You cannot use plastic food container lids (the rubber ones). The cutlery holder is a bit small, but it fits perfectly with my baby's (6-year-old) spoons and forks. For the adults, I just put them inside the dishwasher and ran it. When I removed the top tray, a large wok fits in. Hmm. Also, I was surprised by how much fits in it, much more than I expected. Hot air drying? I heard it was good to have that feature, so I agonized over it for a while before finally buying this one. Even on the basic 75-minute dishwashing function, the door opens automatically. There is a little moisture, but I just wiped it lightly with a dry dishcloth or paper towel. If it’s not urgent, I think it will dry pretty well if I just leave the door a little open. Having never used one before, this is a whole new world. I saw an LG washing machine at another house today, and it wasn't anything special. I heard you only need to do a drum wash about once a month, so I bought a Pringles and plan to do that. I agonized over buying it, but it really is a whole new world that I bought with my own money. Should I say I have more time? For those of you who are debating, the 6-person capacity is sufficient for a family of three. If you gather all the dishes from the day in one go in the evening, it’s enough. Oh! For those wondering about the noise... it’s not unpleasant; it’s about the sound of water filling up in a washing machine. It’s quieter than a vacuum cleaner, quieter than inter-floor noise, and quieter than a baby crying. It’s just about the same level as the water coming out when you’re washing dishes. I'm satisfied. My aunt is the best!

Additional review after Day 1 use: The basic function takes about 75 minutes. You cannot use plastic food container lids (the rubber ones). When I removed the top tray, a large wok fits in. Hmm. Also, I was surprised by how much fits in it, much more than I expected. Hot air drying? I heard it was good to have that feature, so I agonized over it for a while before finally buying this one. Even on the basic 75-minute dishwashing function, the door opens automatically. Having never used one before, this is a whole new world. I saw an LG washing machine at another house today, and it wasn't anything special. I heard you only need to do a drum wash about once a month, so I bought a Pringles and plan to do that. I agonized over buying it, but it really is a whole new world that I bought with my own money. Should I say I have more time? For those of you who are debating, the 6-person capacity is sufficient for a family of three. If you gather all the dishes from the day in one go in the evening, it’s enough. Oh! For those wondering about the noise... it’s not unpleasant; it’s about the sound of water filling up in a washing machine. It’s quieter than a vacuum cleaner, quieter than inter-floor noise, and quieter than a baby crying. It’s just about the same level as the water coming out when you’re washing dishes. I'm satisfied. My aunt is the best!

Should I say I have more time? For those of you who are debating, the 6-person capacity is sufficient for a family of three. Additional review after Day 1 use: The basic function takes about 75 minutes. You cannot use plastic food container lids (the rubber ones). The cutlery holder is a bit small, but it fits perfectly with my baby's (6-year-old) spoons and forks. For the adults, I just put them inside the dishwasher and ran it. When I removed the top tray, a large wok fits in. Hmm. Also, I was surprised by how much fits in it, much more than I expected. Hot air drying? I heard it was good to have that feature, so I agonized over it for a while before finally buying this one. Even on the basic 75-minute dishwashing function, the door opens automatically. There is a little moisture, but I just wiped it lightly with a dry dishcloth or paper towel. If it’s not urgent, I think it will dry pretty well if I just leave the door a little open. Having never used one before, this is a whole new world. I saw an LG washing machine at another house today, and it wasn't anything special. I heard you only need to do a drum wash about once a month, so I bought a Pringles and plan to do that. I agonized over buying it, but it really is a whole new world that I bought with my own money. Should I say I have more time? For those of you who are debating, the 6-person capacity is sufficient for a family of three. If you gather all the dishes from the day in one go in the evening, it’s enough. Oh! For those wondering about the noise... it’s not unpleasant; it’s about the sound of water filling up in a washing machine. My aunt is the best!

So, to make life a little easier, I brought in a "dishwasher lady." Since I bought it with my own money, I wanted to be careful. I debated between the 8-place, 12-place, and 14-place models available on the market. However, given my personality—I can't stand seeing dishes pile up—I'd rather run it one more time than do it all at once. (I'm such a fuss!) I settled on the 6-place model. I watched YouTube and Naver blogs, and I spent two whole days researching before making a decision. Although Coupang offers a 2-year warranty, it was honestly an unfamiliar brand to me. To be cautious, I looked up a lot of reviews before buying. I looked at L, Sam, Coupang, Mi, S... and I decided on this one. Someone once told me that as long as the dishwashing function works well, the brand doesn't really matter. So, I decided on a product that is a bit cheaper but offers great value for money. Advantages of the Midea Dishwasher: 1. It has a 2-tier rack inside that separates, allowing large pots and bulky dishes to fit inside. 2. Its compact size allows for installation even in narrow spaces. 3. It can be installed in the kitchen without drilling holes. 4. It adds a great touch to your interior decor. 5. It saves water. Based on my criteria, I hesitated a lot because it doesn't have UV sterilization or hot air drying. While UV sterilization is nice to have, I didn't find it that great when I used a baby bottle sterilizer. Also, since my baby is currently 6 years old, I felt it wouldn't be necessary, so I passed on it. People said the hot air drying feature is a game changer and is great to have, but opinions are divided, so I passed on that too. I saw reviews saying it's basically drying with a folding dryer. It has an automatic door opening function, so I passed on that as well. If I were to weigh every single factor and buy one that perfectly suits my taste, there would be no end to the choices and the price would go up. I had a benchmark of exactly around the 400,000 won mark. That is why I chose it. It has automatic door opening and allows you to put items in the middle, so... well, it's better than washing dishes by hand. I set the price at 400,000 won and got drill-free installation, so I'm very satisfied in my own way. For those of you considering a dishwasher, I recommend getting one right away. I used to think, "It would be convenient to have, but how much convenience could I really make?" But it is definitely convenient and cleans thoroughly. I think all dishwashers are pretty much the same. I am a family of three who cooks all our meals at home; it is sufficient for one baby and two adults. I hope my review is helpful~~~. Additional review after Day 1 use: The basic function takes about 75 minutes. You cannot use plastic food container lids (the rubber ones). The cutlery holder is a bit small, but it fits perfectly with my baby's (6-year-old) spoons and forks. For the adults, I just put them inside the dishwasher and ran it. When I removed the top tray, a large wok fits in. Hmm. Also, I was surprised by how much fits in it, much more than I expected. Hot air drying? I heard it was good to have that feature, so I agonized over it for a while before finally buying this one. Even on the basic 75-minute dishwashing function, the door opens automatically. There is a little moisture, but I just wiped it lightly with a dry dishcloth or paper towel. If it’s not urgent, I think it will dry pretty well if I just leave the door a little open. Having never used one before, this is a whole new world. I saw an LG washing machine at another house today, and it wasn't anything special. I heard you only need to do a drum wash about once a month, so I bought a Pringles and plan to do that. I agonized over buying it, but it really is a whole new world that I bought with my own money. Should I say I have more time? For those of you who are debating, the 6-person capacity is sufficient for a family of three. If you gather all the dishes from the day in one go in the evening, it’s enough. Oh! For those wondering about the noise... it’s not unpleasant; it’s about the sound of water filling up in a washing machine. It’s quieter than a vacuum cleaner, quieter than inter-floor noise, and quieter than a baby crying. It’s just about the same level as the water coming out when you’re washing dishes. I'm satisfied. My aunt is the best!

So, to make life a little easier, I brought in a "dishwasher lady." Since I bought it with my own money, I wanted to be careful. I debated between the 8-place, 12-place, and 14-place models available on the market. However, given my personality—I can't stand seeing dishes pile up—I'd rather run it one more time than do it all at once. (I'm such a fuss!) I settled on the 6-place model. I watched YouTube and Naver blogs, and I spent two whole days researching before making a decision. Although Coupang offers a 2-year warranty, it was honestly an unfamiliar brand to me. To be cautious, I looked up a lot of reviews before buying. I looked at L, Sam, Coupang, Mi, S... and I decided on this one. Someone once told me that as long as the dishwashing function works well, the brand doesn't really matter. So, I decided on a product that is a bit cheaper but offers great value for money. Advantages of the Midea Dishwasher: 1. It has a 2-tier rack inside that separates, allowing large pots and bulky dishes to fit inside. 2. Its compact size allows for installation even in narrow spaces. 3. It can be installed in the kitchen without drilling holes. 4. It adds a great touch to your interior decor. 5. It saves water. Based on my criteria, I hesitated a lot because it doesn't have UV sterilization or hot air drying. While UV sterilization is nice to have, I didn't find it that great when I used a baby bottle sterilizer. Also, since my baby is currently 6 years old, I felt it wouldn't be necessary, so I passed on it. People said the hot air drying feature is a game changer and is great to have, but opinions are divided, so I passed on that too. I saw reviews saying it's basically drying with a folding dryer. It has an automatic door opening function, so I passed on that as well. If I were to weigh every single factor and buy one that perfectly suits my taste, there would be no end to the choices and the price would go up. I had a benchmark of exactly around the 400,000 won mark. That is why I chose it. It has automatic door opening and allows you to put items in the middle, so... well, it's better than washing dishes by hand. I set the price at 400,000 won and got drill-free installation, so I'm very satisfied in my own way. For those of you considering a dishwasher, I recommend getting one right away. I used to think, "It would be convenient to have, but how much convenience could I really make?" But it is definitely convenient and cleans thoroughly. I think all dishwashers are pretty much the same. I am a family of three who cooks all our meals at home; it is sufficient for one baby and two adults. I hope my review is helpful~~~. Additional review after Day 1 use: The basic function takes about 75 minutes. You cannot use plastic food container lids (the rubber ones). The cutlery holder is a bit small, but it fits perfectly with my baby's (6-year-old) spoons and forks. For the adults, I just put them inside the dishwasher and ran it. When I removed the top tray, a large wok fits in. Hmm. Also, I was surprised by how much fits in it, much more than I expected. Hot air drying? I heard it was good to have that feature, so I agonized over it for a while before finally buying this one. Even on the basic 75-minute dishwashing function, the door opens automatically. There is a little moisture, but I just wiped it lightly with a dry dishcloth or paper towel. If it’s not urgent, I think it will dry pretty well if I just leave the door a little open. Having never used one before, this is a whole new world. I saw an LG washing machine at another house today, and it wasn't anything special. I heard you only need to do a drum wash about once a month, so I bought a Pringles and plan to do that. I agonized over buying it, but it really is a whole new world that I bought with my own money. Should I say I have more time? For those of you who are debating, the 6-person capacity is sufficient for a family of three. If you gather all the dishes from the day in one go in the evening, it’s enough. Oh! For those wondering about the noise... it’s not unpleasant; it’s about the sound of water filling up in a washing machine. It’s quieter than a vacuum cleaner, quieter than inter-floor noise, and quieter than a baby crying. It’s just about the same level as the water coming out when you’re washing dishes. I'm satisfied. My aunt is the best!

Should I say I have more time? For those of you who are debating, the 6-person capacity is sufficient for a family of three. So, to make life a little easier, I brought in a "dishwasher lady." Since I bought it with my own money, I wanted to be careful. I debated between the 8-place, 12-place, and 14-place models available on the market. However, given my personality—I can't stand seeing dishes pile up—I'd rather run it one more time than do it all at once. (I'm such a fuss!) I settled on the 6-place model. I watched YouTube and Naver blogs, and I spent two whole days researching before making a decision. Although Coupang offers a 2-year warranty, it was honestly an unfamiliar brand to me. To be cautious, I looked up a lot of reviews before buying. I looked at L, Sam, Coupang, Mi, S... and I decided on this one. Someone once told me that as long as the dishwashing function works well, the brand doesn't really matter. So, I decided on a product that is a bit cheaper but offers great value for money. Advantages of the Midea Dishwasher: 1. It has a 2-tier rack inside that separates, allowing large pots and bulky dishes to fit inside. 2. Its compact size allows for installation even in narrow spaces. 3. It can be installed in the kitchen without drilling holes. 4. It adds a great touch to your interior decor. 5. It saves water. Based on my criteria, I hesitated a lot because it doesn't have UV sterilization or hot air drying. While UV sterilization is nice to have, I didn't find it that great when I used a baby bottle sterilizer. Also, since my baby is currently 6 years old, I felt it wouldn't be necessary, so I passed on it. People said the hot air drying feature is a game changer and is great to have, but opinions are divided, so I passed on that too. I saw reviews saying it's basically drying with a folding dryer. It has an automatic door opening function, so I passed on that as well. If I were to weigh every single factor and buy one that perfectly suits my taste, there would be no end to the choices and the price would go up. I had a benchmark of exactly around the 400,000 won mark. That is why I chose it. I set the price at 400,000 won and got drill-free installation, so I'm very satisfied in my own way. For those of you considering a dishwasher, I recommend getting one right away. I used to think, "It would be convenient to have, but how much convenience could I really make?" But it is definitely convenient and cleans thoroughly. I think all dishwashers are pretty much the same. I am a family of three who cooks all our meals at home; it is sufficient for one baby and two adults. I hope my review is helpful~~~. Additional review after Day 1 use: The basic function takes about 75 minutes. You cannot use plastic food container lids (the rubber ones). The cutlery holder is a bit small, but it fits perfectly with my baby's (6-year-old) spoons and forks. For the adults, I just put them inside the dishwasher and ran it. When I removed the top tray, a large wok fits in. Hmm. Also, I was surprised by how much fits in it, much more than I expected. Hot air drying? I heard it was good to have that feature, so I agonized over it for a while before finally buying this one. Even on the basic 75-minute dishwashing function, the door opens automatically. There is a little moisture, but I just wiped it lightly with a dry dishcloth or paper towel. If it’s not urgent, I think it will dry pretty well if I just leave the door a little open. Having never used one before, this is a whole new world. I saw an LG washing machine at another house today, and it wasn't anything special. I heard you only need to do a drum wash about once a month, so I bought a Pringles and plan to do that. I agonized over buying it, but it really is a whole new world that I bought with my own money. Should I say I have more time? For those of you who are debating, the 6-person capacity is sufficient for a family of three. If you gather all the dishes from the day in one go in the evening, it’s enough. Oh! For those wondering about the noise... it’s not unpleasant; it’s about the sound of water filling up in a washing machine. It’s quieter than a vacuum cleaner, quieter than inter-floor noise, and quieter than a baby crying. It’s just about the same level as the water coming out when you’re washing dishes. I'm satisfied. My aunt is the best!
